sources.name: NIKL 한국어 학습용 어휘 목록 (National Institute of Korean Language), via julienshim/combined_korean_vocabulary_list
sources.note: results.tsv, `nikl_level` column only. The aggregator is MIT for its code and states it does not host the source lists; the data is NIKL's, published under KOGL Type 1 (공공누리 제1유형), which permits derivatives and commercial use with attribution. The `topik_level` column is NOT used: TOPIK's own terms reserve those rights. The `explanation` column is a collocation hint, not a gloss, and is unused.

sources.name: Open Yonsei Korean Vocabulary (Amulopapa67), a community companion to the six-volume Yonsei course, not affiliated with Yonsei University
sources.note: vol-01.json … vol-06.json. Definitions, text readings, and the course level (the first volume a word appears in). The project licenses its data CC BY-SA 3.0 and excludes textbook lessons, examples, audio and official artwork.

meta.note: Two lists. NIKL grades words A to C; Yonsei places them by the volume of the course that introduces them. Where a word has no definition the popover says so, and the word still marks. Homograph senses (가구03, 가구04) merge into one entry at the easiest grade.
